alignments.note: Impersonal *It* opening the verbless clause. Rule 20 excludes a cleft or impersonal *it* from the construction-supplied frame (only a presentative *there* joins it), so no morpheme licenses this word and it is `added`; the copula *is* beside it goes to the prepositional predicate under rule 49.

The `לְ` heads the prepositional predicate of a verbless clause, so under rule 49 it takes the construction-supplied copula *is* along with its own *for*, headed on the preposition. Unit discontinuous around the `אַל`'s *not* under rule 25.

Vocative proper name; the supplied *O* joins the noun's own unit under rule 36 and is not `added`. Headed on the name, which carries the lexeme.
Second prohibitive `אַל` → *not*; the repetition is written in both languages, so rule 22 does not reach it.
Second impersonal *it*, `added` on the same ground as t001 (rule 20).
Second `לְ` heading the prepositional predicate takes the supplied copula *is* with its own *for* under rule 49, discontinuous around *not* under rule 25.

Bare infinitive construct with no preposition before it, so the English infinitive marker *to* belongs to the infinitive's own unit under rule 52's closing paragraph, headed on the lexical verb.

The waw takes the connective the ASV wrote for it (rule 14). *Nor* here rests on a negative gapped from the preceding lines rather than on a written `לֹא`/`אַל` in this clause, so under rule 35 the single word goes to the waw, which is the only morpheme actually present.

The italicized *to say* supplies a lexical verb for a line whose Hebrew writes none; rule 34's gapping clause covers only the copula, and a supplied lexical verb is `added` under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause. The ASV italic corroborates without deciding it (rule 7).

Interrogative `אֵי` is the predicate of the verbless clause, so it takes the construction-supplied copula *is* along with its own *Where*, exactly as rule 20 gives the *is* of `מִי הָאִישׁ הַלָּזֶה` → *What man is this* to `מִי`. Headed on the wh-word carrying the lexeme.

One substantive rendered by a two-word English phrase (rule 31). Headed on *strong*, since *drink* alone is any drink and is the generic the ASV supplies to complete the phrase; the competing reading heads on *drink* as the class noun, and that alternative is defensible if *drink* is read as realizing the lexeme with *strong* a specifier.

review_notes: The marginal note (*Another reading is, to desire strong drink*) was read and set aside under rule 38: the printed text governs, so the italic *to say* is what is aligned.

The two *It is* frames are divided as rule 49 plus rule 20 direct: the copula joins the `לְ` heading the prepositional predicate and the impersonal *It* is `added`. The competing reading takes *It is* as a single supplied frame on the preposition; that was rejected because rule 20 names a cleft or impersonal *it* as licensed by no morpheme.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV renders the princes' words as a question, "Where is strong drink?", which is the interrogative qere אֵי. The mapped textual_variant note "Another reading is, to desire strong drink" reports the ketiv או (read as a desiderative) as the alternative the ASV did not put in its text, so the note confirms rather than unsettles the choice: the rendered reading is the qere.
